By "suspicious money movements" and "high-risk transactions," I mean transactions that exhibit patterns indicative of potential money laundering. These include wallets with a low age (less than 30 days), high turnover rates (greater than 5), a significant number of linked transactions (3 or more), and a high TCR score (a composite score calculated from transaction chain length, linked transaction count, and fraud probability, exceeding 150). These criteria help identify transactions that deviate from normal behavior and may require further investigation.

CREATE TABLE high_risk_transactions AS
SELECT 
    t.txregistry AS transaction_id,
    t.eventstamp AS transaction_date,
    t.payamtusd AS amount_usd,
    r.txchainlen AS transaction_chain_length,
    r.linkedtxcount AS linked_transaction_count,
    r.fraudprob AS fraud_probability,
    r.wallage AS wallet_age,
    r.wallturnrt AS wallet_turnover_rate,
    (r.txchainlen + r.linkedtxcount + (r.fraudprob * 100)) AS tcr_score
FROM 
    transactions t
JOIN 
    riskanalysis r ON t.txregistry = r.txref
WHERE 
    r.wallage < 30
    AND r.wallturnrt > 5
    AND r.linkedtxcount >= 3
    AND (r.txchainlen + r.linkedtxcount + (r.fraudprob * 100)) > 150;
